chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Khuzaymah told us, saying: Abu Musa told us, saying: Abdul Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan narrated, from Al-A'mash, from Suleiman ibn Meshar, from Kharash ibn al-Harr, from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said:

Three people to whom God will not speak: the one who mentions his favor whenever he gives something, the one who drags down his garment (in arrogance), and the one who sells his goods with false oaths.

key_terms.الْحَلِفُ الْفَاجِرُ: False or wicked oath used in trade
key_terms.الْمُسْبِلُ إِزَارَهُ: One who drags his lower garment in arrogance
key_terms.الْمُنَانُ: One who gives with reluctance and mentions his favor to expect gratitude

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people God will not speak to according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights three distinct forms of spiritual corruption: internal hypocrisy (al-munan), external arrogance (al-musbil), and commercial dishonesty (al-munfiq). In Shia scholarship, these are often interpreted as failures in sincerity, humility, and truthfulness, respectively, which sever the bond of divine communication on the Day of Judgment. The inclusion of 'al-munfiq' specifically links this triad to the broader ethical framework of trade and social interaction emphasized in the Imams' teachings.
